lead.t: Tumour lysis syndrome (TLS) prophylaxis – start aggressive IV hydration (target urine output ≥ 80 ml/h); give allopurinol or rasburicase (if high uric acid) before chemotherapy.

snip.t: Tumour lysis syndrome (TLS) prophylaxis – start aggressive IV hydration (target urine output ≥ 80 ml/h); give allopurinol or rasburicase (if high uric acid) before chemotherapy.
Tumour lysis syndrome – acute renal failure, electrolyte disturbances; mitigated by prophylaxis.
Tumour lysis syndrome: Early cycles — Rising uric acid, hyper‑K, falling Ca — Aggressive hydration, uric acid‑lowering agents, electrolyte correction
*Answer:* Start aggressive IV hydration and allopurinol to prevent tumour lysis syndrome, and give prophylactic TMP‑SMX for PCP because of impending immunosuppression.

Burkitt lymphoma: short, intensive multi-agent chemotherapy; the fastest-growing human tumour, so start treatment urgently and prevent tumour lysis syndrome (hydration, allopurinol or rasburicase, monitoring of potassium, phosphate, calcium and creatinine).
Tumour lysis syndrome: hyperkalaemia, hyperphosphataemia, hypocalcaemia, hyperuricaemia and acute kidney injury.
Serum uric acid and electrolytes (potassium, phosphate, calcium) — baseline before treatment, screening for tumour lysis syndrome risk given rapid cell turnover
